newsitem.title: UK: Powell Duffryn sees progress despite stg.
newsitem.headline: Powell Duffryn sees progress despite stg.

text.p: British ports and engineering company Powell Duffryn said on Thursday that it was confident of further progress in the year ahead "despite the challenges posed by the stronger pound".
The company reported a 4.5 percent rise in pre-tax profits before exceptionals of 44.1 million stg in the year to March 31, along with an unchanged total dividend of 25 pence a share.

It previously announced that it would incur an exceptional charge of 14.3 million stg for 1996/97 on select disposals it was making to focus on its core ports and engineering business. The group has made 10 disposals since March 1996.
"Our principal businesses all have undeniable strengths in their respective fields," chairman Sir Noel Davies said in the results statement.
"Despite the challenges posed by the stronger pound we remain optimistic that further progress will be achieved in the year ahead.
The stronger pound began to have an impact on performance in the second half of the year, especially on the engineering side, although these companies made progress over in the year.

Also, with significant profits derived from the Netherlands and Denmark, the translation effect on overseas earnings had an adverse impact on 1996/97 pre-tax profit approaching 1.0 million stg, said chief executive Barry Hartiss.
"The reshaping of Powell Duffryn is making good progress," said Hartiss.

"Management action will continue to eliminate weaknesses, capitalise on existing strengths and identify appropriate opportunities to strengthen the portfolio still further. With this clear agenda we look to the future with growing optimism".
